clue.text: Bob found a way to save time

definitions.meaning: a bob is a hairstyle cropped level and brief
a quicker route or method than the usual one

explanation.surface: Someone discovered how to get somewhere faster.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a cropped haircut, and a quicker route that saves time is the other sense of the same phrase.

clue.text: Had included odd pieces of cake (a quarter) that had been cut

indicators.note: the word had holds the other letters within it, as something included is enclosed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first and third letters of the word cake, its odd-numbered positions

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A slice of cake has been taken out of a whole one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd pieces of' takes C and K from 'cake'; with E (a compass quarter) they sit inside HAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hacked has been chopped roughly, so it is a past-tense synonym for being cut.

clue.text: Car perhaps, one spotted by bishop outside

indicators.note: the bishop's letters stand on either side, enclosing the other piece

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation for a bishop
an ace is the single spot on a die or playing card

explanation.surface: A bishop notices a car going past.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is styled the Right Reverend, abbreviated RR; the ace is the 'one' marked with a single spot on dice and cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A racer is a vehicle built for competing in speed contests, a car being one example.

clue.text: Fickle person coming from a clean home

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are worked into something new, emerging from it in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A changeable character raised in a tidy household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from' rearranges CLEANHOME; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The lizard that changes colour gives its name to anyone who alters opinions to suit company.

clue.text: US author found the gold hidden with more gold

indicators.note: the gold is tucked away inside the word the, held within it

parts.note: taken as written
OR is the heraldic term for gold
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An American writer strikes it rich twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (heraldic gold) goes inside THE, then AU (gold's chemical symbol) follows. Henry David Thoreau wrote Walden.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau was a nineteenth-century American essayist and naturalist.

clue.text: Infer that most of the bird is in the river

indicators.note: the shortened bird sits within the river's letters, placed in the middle

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: the bird loses its final letter, leaving only most of it

parts.note: a duck is a water bird

explanation.surface: A deduction that a duck is swimming in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the bird's last letter and 'is in' sets the rest inside the Dee, a river in Wales and Scotland; 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to reach a conclusion by reasoning, which is what inferring means.

clue.text: Hang down, nothing will fall out

indicators.note: the fall's letters lie outside, enclosing the zero

parts.note: to drop is to fall
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Let something sag, and nothing will tumble from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' puts DROP outside O, giving DR-O-OP.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or hang limply downward.

clue.text: Create odd sort of architectural style

indicators.note: to sort letters is to rearrange them, so the two words are shuffled together

explanation.surface: Invent a strange kind of building design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder: 'sort of' rearranges CREATE plus ODD.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorated Gothic is the name of the ornate English church-building period of the fourteenth century.

clue.text: Drinking vessel on table in the kitchen

definitions.text: Drinking vessel on table in the kitchen

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other, so the vessel comes first

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A mug placed on the kitchen table.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' means the first piece stands above the second; the whole clue also describes where crockery is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard is the kitchen storage unit where cups and plates are shelved.

clue.text: Bill's repeated first-class backing for a tree

indicators.note: the bill's abbreviation is given twice in succession

parts.note: AC, account, is a bill

indicators.note: first-class is turned round so it reads backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone's bill gets backed twice as a first-rate forestry purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' gives ACAC; 'backing' turns A1 (written AI) into IA.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a thorny wattle of warm climates, a genus of trees and shrubs.

clue.text: Too confusing, range used by aural instrument

indicators.note: the letters of the short word are mixed up, as confused things are jumbled

parts.note: scope means range or extent

explanation.surface: An ear device baffles with too much range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too' looks like an adverb, but it is the fodder that 'confusing' scrambles; 'used by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An otoscope is the lighted device a doctor uses to look into the ear canal.

clue.text: Relief about heartless power of one woman

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the inside of the word power is removed, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A woman's power wanes, bringing relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' keeps P and R from 'power'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve is a temporary respite or cancellation of punishment, a relief from it.

clue.text: Table, perhaps, it's something taken for granted

definitions.meaning: a table is one example of household tables and chairs
an idiom for anything so familiar nobody notices it

explanation.surface: A table is so familiar nobody notices it any more.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a table is one item among chairs and sofas; idiomatically the phrase means a fixture so familiar it is overlooked.

clue.text: See 12
Flier got tight rolling round Rome

indicators.note: the letters tumble about, rolled into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot gets drunk on a whirl around the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got' is a link; 'Flier' covers both the vintage biplane and the moth, and 'rolling round' scrambles the two words together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiger Moth is a classic biplane, and also a moth, so either way it flies.

clue.text: Want to see Dennis around

indicators.note: the letters are moved about, scattered into another order

explanation.surface: Wishing to visit Dennis nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges SEEDENNIS; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Neediness is a state of poverty or lack, which is one sense of want as a noun.

clue.text: Pleasure horseman had from driver of stolen vehicle

parts.note: joy is pleasure
a rider is a horseman

explanation.surface: A rider's delight came from a car thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A joyrider takes a car without permission and drives it for thrills.

clue.text: Moving steadily on, counterfeiting only one side of the coin

parts.note: forging is making fakes, counterfeiting

parts.words: only one side of the coin
parts.note: a coin has a head and a tail, so one side is a head

explanation.surface: A forger progresses by faking just one face of a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Heads and tails are the two sides of a coin, so one side gives A HEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To forge ahead is an idiom for making steady progress onward.

clue.text: No object in troubling Melissa

indicators.note: to trouble is to stir up, so the name's letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: There is no reason to bother Melissa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubling' rearranges MELISSA; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless means without purpose, lacking any goal or aim.

clue.text: Lives for clothes?

definitions.meaning: whimsically read, someone who lives does the opposite of dying, an un-dying

explanation.definitionFit: Read as un-dies, the word humorously means does not die, that is, lives; it is also slang for underwear.

clue.text: Boring rubbish to bring the house down?

parts.note: dry means dull, boring
rot means rubbish, nonsense

explanation.surface: A tedious, trashy show that brings the house down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bring the house down' usually means a show earns rapturous applause; here it is literal, a fungus that rots timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a timber-decaying fungus that can make a building collapse.

clue.text: Mark two

definitions.meaning: Mark ..., the pen name of Samuel Clemens

explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Clemens wrote as Mark Twain, and the old word for a pair is the same.

clue.text: Sea route used by trains!

parts.note: the main is the open sea
a line is a route, as a railway line

explanation.surface: A sea lane for trains, absurdly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the sea; the whole clue also describes a railway's trunk route.
explanation.definitionFit: A main line is the principal railway track between major stations.

clue.text: Learning about one European banker

indicators.note: the learning's letters go round the other, about it

parts.note: lore is learning, traditional knowledge
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A scholar studies a single European financier.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is often a river, something with banks; here a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is France's longest river, so a European waterway with banks.

clue.text: Favour man pressing a suit

definitions.meaning: a lawyer pursuing a case in court

explanation.definitionFit: To argue for something is to support it, and a barrister arguing a lawsuit carries the same title.

clue.text: Draw forth priest, Italian, going round chapter

indicators.note: the two joined words encircle the chapter's letter

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel
It is short for Italian, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A priest and an Italian circle a chapter to draw something out.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel; ELI and IT together surround C.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out a response or information.

clue.text: Raggedly-dressed child might be found at sea

definitions.meaning: the spiny marine creature, a sea creature of that name

explanation.definitionFit: A ragged mischievous youngster shares a name with the spiny echinoderm called the sea version.

clue.text: Mounting excitement will point to us to think in French

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point
taken as written
pense is French for thinks

explanation.surface: Excitement builds as someone points to us and thinks in French.
explanation.walkthrough: S (a compass point) goes to US, then PENSE, French for 'thinks'.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is growing tension and anticipation, which is excitement on the rise.
